repo: Sayjad's RusKey reproduction (/root/ruskey in WSL): driver/ruskey_bench.cc, lerp/lerp.py, rocksdb fork v11.8.1 branch ruskey-flsm
status: Reviewed 2026-10-08 by an assistant against the paper and the reproduction's scripts (review/REVIEW.md); not yet signed off by the reproduction author. reproduction_value = the final Figure 6 regime: results_fig6_final2 -> results_monkey20 (go20.sh, wsl_monkey.sh).

evidence.quote: we initially bulk load the empty database with 100 million random sampled key-value entries
4 levels at 20 GB against the paper's 5-6 at 100 GB

assumptions.review_note: Driver default is 100M, but every final Fig. 6 run used 20M (wsl_tuner.sh:27, go20.sh:22), so status is stated_code_differs. Mattered most of all: at 6M keys (fits in RAM) read-heavy K=1 vs K=10 was flat (81.4 vs 81.4 us/op); the K trade-off appeared only at 20M (data > 16 GB RAM).

evidence.quote: --rate_limit_mb N        cap compaction bandwidth at N MB/s (0 = off)
With the cap, K=1 stalls nearly four times as much as K=10.

assumptions.review_note: Final runs leave it off. It mattered at 500K keys: 30 MB/s gave K=1 152.4 us/op with 3187 s of write stalls (RESULTS_LOG.md:1844); dropped once data reached 20 GB.

evidence.quote: we enable direct I/Os for read and write

assumptions.review_note: Driver default is false, but all final runs pass --direct_io (run_experiments.py:259, wsl_monkey.sh, adapt_curve.py), so it effectively matches. Caveat: under WSL2, O_DIRECT doesn't bypass the host's cache (same run: read-heavy lookups 10.6 us vs write-heavy 394.8 us, RESULTS_LOG.md:2570).
Driver default is 64 (ruskey_bench.cc:1275), but final runs use 8 MB (wsl_tuner.sh:71, wsl_monkey.sh) and older runs used 2 MB. Matters: GapFinder's own run moved K10/K5 from 0.87 to 2.74 at 64 MB.
Driver default is 32 (ruskey_bench.cc:151), but final runs use 256 (wsl_tuner.sh:28, go20.sh:22). Filter and index blocks sit outside the cache. The 32 -> 256 effect at 20 GB was never isolated.
Final runs use 4. An old 1/4/8 sweep (500K keys, pre-rewrite engine) didn't change the best K.

Driver default is 0.0, but final runs use 1.0: every lookup misses (wsl_tuner.sh:29, go20.sh:22). Paper: unstated for the experiments, but its cost model analyses the zero-result case (p.13). Mattered: with hit lookups, read-heavy showed no K effect (commit 51c95df).

assumptions.paper_value: false (other levels frozen while training, sec. 5.2.1)
assumptions.review_note: Paper value confirmed (sec. 5.2.1: 'The compaction policies of other levels remain unchanged throughout this process'). But it is a no-op in the final runs: --mode cost (wsl_tuner.sh:73) bypasses Lerp; see the new tuner_mode row.
No-op in the final runs (cost mode, not DDPG); see the new tuner_mode row.

assumptions.paper_value: unstated (no such mechanism in the paper)
assumptions.review_note: No-op in the final runs. It mattered earlier: 0.4 vetoed every move; 0.15 found and held K=10 (commit 805fb50).

evidence.quote: We set the memory buffer size to 2MB, the size ratio to 10, and the default Bloom filter bits-per-key to 8
the default Bloom filter bits-per-key to 8

assumptions.review_note: The paper's Fig. 6 uses uniform 8 bits/key; Monkey with 4 bits/key is Fig. 8's setting (p.15, p.18). Final repro Fig. 6 runs used Monkey 4 bits/key (wsl_monkey.sh, run_experiments.py:117), so status is stated_code_differs. Mattered: write-heavy K=1 minus K=10 went from +7.4 (uniform) to +16.1 us/op (Monkey) (RESULTS_LOG.md:2464, 2527).

evidence.quote: The mission size is set to 50000 operations

assumptions.review_note: Driver default is 50000, but final runs used 40,000 (wsl_tuner.sh:70, adapt_curve.py:42, wsl_monkey.sh), so status is stated_code_differs. Effect not tested.

assumptions.code_default: n/a (reproduction: 16 vCPU, 15 GB RAM, NVMe under WSL2)

evidence.quote: 256GB DDR4 main memory, and 1TB NVMe SSD

assumptions.review_note: Repro detail: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, 16 cores, 15 GB RAM (host 32 GB), ext4 on a virtual disk on NTFS. Mattered: the trade-off needs data larger than RAM, and host caching is the suspected reason balanced settles at K=10.

assumptions.reproduction_value: final runs: 150 per fixed arm, 480 for the tuner
assumptions.review_note: Mattered: on read-heavy the tuner averaged 23.2 us/op vs 10.1 for fixed K=1, because exploration isn't paid back within 480 missions (RESULTS_LOG.md:2620).

assumptions.paper_value: Lerp (DDPG): tune Level 1, other levels unchanged, then propagate (sec. 5.2.1)
assumptions.reproduction_value: final runs: `--mode cost` (online-fitted cost model, settle 30, average 60), one K on every level (wsl_tuner.sh:73)
assumptions.review_note: Mattered: on write-heavy DDPG chose K=4; the cost model chose K=10 (commit 3aed1be).

assumptions.paper_value: p.16 (RocksDB version): sealed runs merge gradually through file compactions triggered by other runs; sec. 4.2: a full level merges all runs to the next level
assumptions.reproduction_value: rocksdb d36167568: a full level merges into the next level's active run
